text: **dsh-plugin-notify-sounds**（DSH 网页与桌面客户端插件）：在审批、提问或任务完成时通过 Web Audio 播放提示音。它由 Host 配置与路由、Client 状态监听和设置页组成；可按事件选九种合成音或最多三个自定义音频，并配置系统通知、标题提醒、静音时段、仅后台提醒、未处理决策重复提醒及目标模式最终轮提醒。通知点击可返回对应 DSH 窗口，设置即时生效。适合离开屏幕工作、但想获知会话待响应或完成状态的用户。无需 API key；自定义音频、系统通知权限和更新检查均可选。

**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** (DSH web/desktop): plays sounds when a session needs input or finishes. Choose per-event cues, quiet hours, hidden-only alerts, repeat reminders, and goal-mode final alerts. Add up to three audio clips; clicked system notifications return to DSH. No API key is required.
智能体等我审批或者回答问题时，能不能提醒我一下？
我不想一直盯着 DSH，任务完成后希望收到提示音。
想给审批和提问分别设置不同的铃声。
晚上休息时，能让 DSH 的提醒在固定时段静音吗？
没看到待处理决策的话，过几分钟再提醒我一次。
我想上传自己喜欢的短音频，作为任务通知声。
目标模式会跑很多轮，能不能只在最后结束时提示？
Alert me when a DSH session needs my approval or finishes while I am away.
Can I set quiet hours and use my own short audio clips for session alerts?
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「合成提示音」功能：使用 Web Audio 播放九种预设音；设置页支持试听，并可为不同事件选择音效。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「会话事件提醒」功能：检测待处理审批、提问出现和会话由运行转为空闲，并分别播放配置的提示音。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「系统通知」功能：页面不可见或窗口失焦时显示会话通知；点击后由 Host 路由尝试唤回 DSH 窗口。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「标题状态标记」功能：页面隐藏时在窗口标题显示待处理或已完成状态，返回页面后清除已读标记。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「静音和后台提醒」功能：可设置每日静音时间段，或只在页面不可见时播放提示音。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「重复决策提醒」功能：对尚未看过的待处理决策按设定分钟间隔重提醒；用户查看后停止重复。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「目标最终轮提醒」功能：开启后等待目标模式完成、暂停或受阻，只在最终阶段提醒而跳过中间轮。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「自定义音频库」功能：上传最多三个短音频，为它们命名并分配给审批、提问或完成事件。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「更新检查」功能：设置页可查询 npm 上的新版本，并在页面加载后按每日频率静默自动检查。
**dsh-plugin-notify-sounds** 的「即改即用设置」功能：在专属 Sounds 设置页调整总开关、音量和各事件选项，配置通过 DSH 表单实时写入。
dsh-plugin-notify-sounds 检查更新时会向 npm 官方 registry 查询版本，必要时也查询 npmmirror；这不是声音播放所需配置。

**A soft chime when the agent is waiting for you — or when it is done.**

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · dsh-plugin-notify-sounds：Walk away from the window without missing anything: an OS notification whether the window is minimised, covered, or merely unfocused (**click it to jump back**), and a "Waiting for you" / "Finished" mark on the taskbar title. Once you have seen it, the plugin goes quiet — it will not nag you like an alarm clock.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · dsh-plugin-notify-sounds：**Install**: DSH → **Plugins** in the left sidebar → Add plugin, paste the line below (keep the version — a release younger than 24 hours is resolved back to the previous one by pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge`) and press **Install**:

```
dsh-plugin-notify-sounds@1.9.4
```

---

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🎨 Consistent with DSH's design language：Every visual detail of the settings section comes from DSH's own design system: row geometry, dividers, type sizes and spacing use the official design tokens, the sound picker is the official `Menu` primitive, the icons come from the official family, and the layout follows the native text-left, control-right row shape. Installing it does not introduce a visually disjoint third-party block into your settings.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 💡 Why：DSH tells you things visually — status dots, sidebar marks. The moment you switch to another window, you can neither see nor hear anything, while the agent may be stuck waiting for one sentence from you.

This plugin turns "it is waiting for you" and "it is done" into sound. With system notifications and the title mark you know what happened even while away; and once you come back and see it, it goes quiet — the repeat reminder only chases decisions you have **never** seen.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🔔 Sounds：Bell · Chime · Ding · Drop · Pulse · Arc · Coin · Success · Knock — nine built-in sounds, all synthesized live with Web Audio: no audio files, no network requests.

Or upload your own audio (mp3 / wav / ogg / m4a, up to 15s and 3MB each, validated and loudness-normalized), or pick "None" for notifications only. Each trigger (approval / question / completion) gets its own sound, with preview right in the settings.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · ⚙️ Settings：Settings → **Sounds** (between General and Models). Every feature has its own toggle, styled exactly like DSH's own preference pages:

master switch and volume · per-trigger sounds with preview · sub-agent alerts · system notifications · window title alert · repeat interval · quiet hours · hidden-only mode · up to three named clips of your own · update checks (installs go through the package manager)

Everything applies immediately — no restart needed.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🖱️ Simplest: two clicks inside DSH (recommended)：1. In DSH open the **Plugins** panel in the left sidebar and press **Add plugin**;
2. Paste the package name **with a version** (this plugin is published on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds)):

```
   dsh-plugin-notify-sounds@1.9.4
   ```

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🖱️ Simplest: two clicks inside DSH (recommended)：Do not drop the version: pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` policy keeps a release younger than 24 hours out of automatic resolution, so the bare name resolves to the previous one. The current version is on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds?activeTab=versions) and in [Releases](https://github.com/BillCx330/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds/releases).
   (The GitHub repository address `https://github.com/BillCx330/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds` or a local directory path work too, but neither pins a version.)
3. Press **Install**, then **restart DSH** once.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🖱️ Simplest: two clicks inside DSH (recommended)：The "install source" dropdown above the box picks the download mirror (mainland China mirror by default; leave it alone unless downloads are slow). DSH warns that a plugin runs with your permissions — this one only reads session state and plays sounds locally; its single request goes to **your own DSH** to raise the window when you click a notification, and nothing is sent anywhere else.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · ⬆️ Upgrading：**Upgrades are installed by the package manager**, so the profile's lockfile moves with the files — a DSH plugin cannot install its own update durably (the manager refuses a package that is already declared, and its remove-then-install step unloads the very code that would finish the install). The plugin therefore only *checks*, and tells you where to install:

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · ⬆️ Upgrading：- **Inside DSH (recommended, and the only path verified on the Desktop)**: **Plugins** in the left sidebar → uninstall this plugin under *Installed plugins* → **Add plugin** → paste `dsh-plugin-notify-sounds@<version>` → Install → restart DSH. (Keep the version: pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` policy keeps a freshly published version out of automatic resolution for its first 24 hours, so the bare name can resolve to the previous release.)

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · ⬆️ Upgrading：Uninstalling keeps your settings: preferences and uploaded audio live in the profile (`cordis.patch.yml` and `notify-sounds/sounds/`), so a reinstall restores them — including a clip migrated out of a pre-1.9.0 install.
- **With the marketplace plugin** ([dshmarket](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dshmarket)): update it in one click there.
- **On a `web` profile**: `dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add dsh-plugin-notify-sounds@<version>`.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · ⬆️ Upgrading：The update row also warns when the running version is not what the profile's lockfile records — the state left behind by the pre-1.8.0 self-updater. One reinstall through the package manager fixes it for good.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🛠️ Other ways：**Command line** — one command against the profile you actually use:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add github:BillCx330/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds
```

(A Git install follows the repository's default branch and pins no version; use `package@version` above when the install has to be reproducible.)

**Release archive** — download the `.tgz` from [Releases](https://github.com/BillCx330/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds/releases) and install it by its **path on disk**:

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🛠️ Other ways：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add ./dsh-plugin-notify-sounds-1.9.4.tgz
```

(`dsh plugin add` hands its argument straight to the package manager, so it takes a local file path — a download URL will not work.)

**Local directory** — for development or trying unreleased changes:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add ./dsh-plugin-notify-sounds
```

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🛠️ Other ways：**By hand** — add `"dsh-plugin-notify-sounds": "github:BillCx330/dsh-plugin-notify-sounds"` to `dependencies` in the profile's `package.json`, append `"dsh-plugin-notify-sounds"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, then run a package install (e.g. `pnpm install`) in the profile directory so the dependency lands in `node_modules`.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🛠️ Other ways：The command line writes `dsh.profile.bundles` and installs the dependency for you. The package ships prebuilt artifacts and declares no lifecycle scripts, so nothing is built at install time. **Restart DSH** after installing (everyday upgrades that touch only the client half hot-reload).

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · ⚠️ Known limitations：- **Where custom audio lives**: each file is stored by content hash under `profiles/<profile>/notify-sounds/sounds/<sha256>.<ext>`, and the config keeps only its name. **Back up (or move) the whole profile directory** — copying `cordis.patch.yml` alone does not carry the audio. After uninstalling, at most the last file stays behind (a few hundred KB).
- **Hand-edited config**: preferences live in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`; values must match the schema (volume 0–100, a preset id, `HH:MM` times) or the plugin declines to load — just fix the value. The settings UI only ever writes valid values.
- **Upgrades are installed by the package manager, not by the plugin**: 1.8.0 removed the self-installer (writing files in place never updated the profile's lockfile, so the next plugin install silently restored the old version). The update row still checks npm and reports a newer version, then points at the route that installs — the **Plugins** panel in the sidebar (uninstall, then add again), the marketplace, or `dsh plugin add` on a web profile.

dsh-plugin-notify-sounds README · 🧩 Design notes：- **Triggers never touch the event waterfall**: approval/question requests are waterfall events that a late listener can miss, so this plugin reads `uiSession.sessionStatus` (the same aggregated pending/running facts the sidebar status dots use) and just observes.
- **Repeat cadence**: unanswered decisions are checked every 15s; **seen means done** — appearing while you are at the window, or coming back to it, ends the reminders for good (switching away does not re-arm); a new question replacing an old one resets the timer. A reminder that comes due during quiet hours is dropped rather than deferred.
- **Click-to-return**: a renderer cannot raise an OS window, so a click POSTs to the Host's fenced `/notify-sounds/focus` route and the Host raises it. On Windows the Host calls `user32.dll` through DSH's own bundled `koffi` (no new dependency, window calls only, no PowerShell — that shape trips security software and gets blamed on DSH); Desktop vs browser is derived from the `Origin` header, so a browser click never drags the Desktop window forward.

npm install             # once: the Host tests need the schemastery devDependency
node test/smoke.mjs     # client half: assembly, triggers, cooldown, quiet hours, repeat reminders, notification clicks, sub-agent filtering

To publish to npm: bump the version, then `npm publish` (`npm login` and 2FA the first time). **npm versions are immutable** — bump for every change.
